papers.title: Antarctic sea ice variability and monsoonal precipitation: a review of reported teleconnections, associations and uncertainties
papers.journal: Progress in Earth and Planetary Science
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“极地气候”：标题或摘要命中 antarctic、sea ice、southern annular mode、southern ocean、climate，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract Antarctic sea ice variability is increasingly recognized as a potentially important component of the coupled Southern Hemisphere climate system. Growing observational, reanalysis, and modeling evidence suggests that Antarctic sea ice anomalies are associated with large-scale atmospheric circulation changes that may contribute to climate variability in tropical and subtropical regions. However, the relative contribution of Antarctic sea ice variability compared with established climate drivers such as the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) and the Southern Annular Mode (SAM) remains incompletely understood. At the sectoral scale, asymmetric sea ice variability associated with wind-driven Ekman transport, air–sea heat flux anomalies, and ocean–ice interactions has been linked to dipole-like patterns of atmospheric and oceanic variability that may alter jet streams, storm tracks, and large-scale circulation. Proposed teleconnection pathways involving Rossby wave propagation and circulation adjustments suggest that sea ice variability in the Indian Ocean, Pacific, and Atlantic sectors may be associated with changes in cross-equatorial moisture transport, subtropical jet position, and regional pressure systems, with potential implications for precipitation variability across South Asia, East Asia, and Africa. Collectively, the available evidence indicates that Antarctic sea ice variability may represent one component of a broader interconnected climate system influencing hydroclimatic variability across multiple regions, while also highlighting substantial uncertainties regarding the magnitude, mechanisms, and regional expression of these relationships. Improved understanding of Southern Ocean–ice–atmosphere interactions and their representation in climate models will be important for evaluating the potential role of Antarctic sea ice variability in seasonal-to-decadal climate variability and hydroclimatic predictability.

papers.title: High resolution sediment-specific surface soil moisture retrieval using Sentinel-1 time series and auxiliary data
papers.journal: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“AI × 气候”：标题或摘要命中 machine learning、shap、temperature、weather，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: In this study, we examine the potential of continuous ground moisture monitoring over a mining site using a combination of in-situ soil moisture sensors and multi-sensor SAR images. We focus on assessing and improving methodologies for retrieval of surface soil moisture, i.e. ground moisture, from SAR measurements focusing on detailed in situ reference observations for several key geomaterials, i.e. sediments, typical in the study site. The mining site represents a limestone quarry located in the southeastern Finland. Our hypothesis is that sediment-specific well-calibrated models can be instrumental in improving soil moisture retrieval under different weather conditions to produce spatially explicit soil moisture estimates at high resolution compared to baseline approaches. Studied SAR data are represented by Copernicus Sentinel-1 C-band images, while auxiliary datasets include optical Sentinel-2 data. Reference data were collected using IoT enabled capacitance sensors. The reference data were calibrated based on laboratory analyses conducted on the different sediment types studied, including organic soil, clay, gravel, and flotation sand. The examined machine learning (ML) methods include XGBoost, LightGBM, random forest, support vector regression, linear regression and k-nearest neighbors. The performance of ML algorithms was evaluated using different cross-validation techniques including a five-fold approach as well as Leave-One-Sensor-Out (LOSO) to assess predictive accuracy and transferability to unseen sensors. The best performance under random five-fold cross-validation was achieved with the most comprehensive feature set which combines Sentinel-1 backscatter, time-series based soil moisture indices (SMI), Sentinel-2 optical, topographic, and temperature predictors. SHAP analysis revealed that SAR based features such as VH backscatter, traditional SMI derived from VV backscatter, and incidence angle were among the most important multi-source predictors. Adding sediment information improved Sentinel-1-only retrievals by more than 2 vol-%, but provided little additional benefit when richer multi-source feature sets were used. In the best sediment-area-level configurations, RMSE decreased to 0.037–0.050 m 3 m − 3 (3.7-5.0 vol. % points ), with R 2 values reaching 0.90. Accuracy varied by sediment texture, with the lowest errors for clay and organic soil and higher errors for flotation sand and gravel. However, LOSO validation demonstrated substantially weaker and site-dependent transferability: R 2 ranged from 0.45 to 0.67 for organic soil at a southern site and from 0.07 to 0.21 for organic soil at a northern site. Thus, high within-dataset predictive accuracy did not translate uniformly to unseen sensor locations, highlighting the need for broader spatially independent validation.

papers.title: Extreme glacier melt on the Central Tibetan Plateau during the summer of 2022: detection and mechanisms
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 tibetan plateau、plateau、climate、atmospher、weather，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Extreme glacier melt events accelerate mass loss, increase glacier instability, and temporarily increase downstream runoff, potentially alleviating drought conditions. Yet the glacier energy–mass balance in the Geladandong region – a headwater region of the Yangtze River (China's longest river) and one of the source regions feeding Siling Co (Tibet's largest lake) – and its connection to the unprecedented 2022 summer melt remain insufficiently quantified. To address this gap, we integrated in-situ mass balance observations and glacio-meteorological data from a 5700 m monitoring site with an energy-mass balance model and applied a novel dual-threshold framework (based on mean and standard deviation) to identify extreme mass loss/melt events in short-term glacier mass balance records. Our novel methodology identified 2021/22 as a period of extreme mass loss and melt intensity, with melt during the 2022 summer heatwave reaching unprecedented extremes. These heatwaves caused an increase in melt amount of 317.8 mm w.e., amounting to 1.66 and 1.69 times the values recorded for the same period in 2019/20 and 2020/21, respectively. This extreme melt was driven by energy balance anomalies over the glacier surface. In terms of net contributions to the +28.2 W m −2 melt energy anomaly during the three identified heatwave windows, enhanced sensible heat flux was the largest term (+17.0 W m −2 ; 60.3 %), followed by increased net longwave radiation (+14.0 W m −2 ; 49.7 %) and increased net shortwave radiation (+5.1 W m −2 ; 18.1 %) associated with reduced albedo, with negative contributions from latent heat flux and subsurface heat flux. Such anomalies were driven by large-scale atmospheric circulation patterns, specifically the eastward extension and northward displacement of the South Asian High (SAH), together with near-neutral mid-latitude westerlies. This study advances the understanding of glacier mass balance responses to extreme weather and climate events on the central Tibetan Plateau.

papers.title: Discovering Equations for the Thermodynamics of South Asian Monsoon Precipitation
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“AI × 气候”：标题或摘要命中 neural network、ocean、monsoon、precipitation，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: South Asian monsoon precipitation depends on the thermodynamic structure of the lower troposphere, but how its ingredients combine to shape precipitation remains unclear, partly because this dependence is nonlocal in the vertical. We use symbolic distillation, which combines neural networks and symbolic regression, to discover interpretable precipitation equations from 21 years of June-August reanalysis data. Neural networks first learn the vertical thermodynamic structure most relevant to precipitation, condensing each variable into a single interpretable feature not tied to a particular vertical grid. Then, symbolic regression derives closed-form equations from these features and the surface state. Our best equation explains 1.5 times as much precipitation variance as a widely used buoyancy-based diagnostic and recovers about 85% of neural network skill while using about a thousand times fewer parameters. Unlike the buoyancy diagnostic, which adds moisture and instability, the equations treat them as competing controls, with the heaviest precipitation occurring when the lower free troposphere is humid. Over ocean, sensible heating is associated with additional precipitation mainly when near-surface air is warm and moist, improving predicted precipitation and its diurnal cycle. Although the learned features were optimized only for precipitation prediction, the equations largely respond to each feature as expected from convective physics, consistent with the reanalysis. These responses reduce the dependence of monsoon precipitation on the entire vertical column to a few simple, testable constraints that could guide data-driven precipitation models to make them more physically consistent.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Hourly Land–Atmosphere Interaction Dataset from a Coordinated 15-Station Network Spanning the Environmental Gradients of the Tibetan Plateau (2021–24)
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 tibetan plateau、plateau、atmospher、monsoon、temperature，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract Accurate characterization of land–atmosphere interactions over the Tibetan Plateau (TP) is hindered by fragmented measurements, inconsistent data-processing standards, and a scarcity of integrated, multi-component observations. To address these limitations, we present an integrated dataset from 15 stations spanning monsoon-dominated, westerlies-dominated, and transitional regions of the TP. The dataset features hourly gradient meteorological variables, radiation components, soil temperature and moisture measurements, and turbulent fluxes, providing vertically resolved information on land surface processes. Processed under standardized protocols with harmonized temporal resolutions, consistent variable definitions, and rigorous quality control procedures, the data ensure high reliability and internal consistency. This dataset provides a robust observational foundation for advancing process-based understanding of land–atmosphere coupling and its representation in models over the TP. It is expected to support land surface and Earth system model evaluation, satellite product validation, and data assimilation. Furthermore, it provides a basis for developing hybrid physics-machine learning approaches for data quality control and gap-filling in-situ observations in complex high-altitude environments.

papers.title: Selective coupling of the Western Tibetan Vortex and the South Asian High
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“青藏高原”：标题或摘要命中 tibetan plateau、plateau、atmospher、circulation，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract The Western Tibetan Vortex (WTV) and South Asian High (SAH) overlap in the Asian upper troposphere, but whether they represent distinct phenomena and how they interact remain unclear. Using ERA5 reanalysis (1979–2023) and 53 CMIP6 models, we demonstrate that the WTV is a year-round circulation-variability mode distinct from the summer SAH anticyclone. Their summer variability is selectively coupled through SAH position rather than intensity or extent, with SAH centre displacements explaining 52.8% of WTV variance. This relationship involves two complementary pathways: meridional displacement associated with subtropical westerly jet shifts and zonal displacement associated with circulation anomalies over the western Tibetan Plateau. We further show that WTV variability covaries with the continuous western ridge of the SAH, but not with intermittent splitting into separate centres. Most CMIP6 models reproduce the coupling structure but underestimate its strength. These findings clarify the dynamical relationship between two distinct atmospheric phenomena and resolve a longstanding ambiguity surrounding the SAH western centre.

papers.title: A Causal Effect Network Analysis of Summer Compound Heatwave and Drought Events Over the Yangtze River Basin
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“东亚气候”：标题或摘要命中 yangtze、atmospher、temperature、circulation、radiation，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract Under global warming, compound heatwave and drought events (CHDEs) have become increasingly frequent. Although large‐scale atmospheric circulation and land–atmosphere feedback are recognized as the primary drivers of CHDEs, the strengths of their causal relationships and long‐term evolution remain poorly quantified. Focusing on summer CHDEs over the Yangtze River Basin (YRB) during 1961–2022, this study uses the ERA5 reanalysis data set and the Peter and Clark Momentary Conditional Independence (PCMCI) causal discovery method to construct causal effect networks for both individual extreme events and CHDEs, and quantitatively investigates the strengths and long‐term evolution of the identified causal pathways. The results show that large‐scale circulation anomalies not only directly promote regional warming but also induce soil drying, providing a favorable large‐scale atmospheric background for CHDEs. Soil moisture (SM) maintains drought conditions through a pronounced memory effect and further enhances near‐surface warming via land–atmosphere feedback, resulting in stronger atmosphere–land coupling during compound events than during individual heat events. Accordingly, both circulation anomalies and SM deficits are stronger in CHDEs than in individual heat events. Long‐term analysis shows that large‐scale circulation has remained the dominant and relatively stable driver of regional heat extremes and CHDEs, whereas the influence of SM on temperature has strengthened significantly, with the enhancement during compound events being approximately twice that for individual extreme events. This strengthening is associated with declining SM, suppressed evapotranspiration, and an enhanced conversion of net radiation from latent to sensible heat flux over the YRB.

papers.title: Dynamical precursors to summer temperature extremes on the Antarctic Peninsula
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“极地气候”：标题或摘要命中 antarctic、southern annular mode、temperature、circulation，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Extreme warm summer near-surface temperatures over the Antarctic Peninsula (AP) can lead to surface melting and the disintegration of ice shelves. While individual case studies have linked such events to anomalous large-scale circulation, a systematic assessment of the dynamical pathways leading to AP-wide extreme austral summer warm events remains limited. This study uses ERA5 reanalysis data to investigate the large-scale dynamical precursors associated with extreme warm days over the Antarctic Peninsula. We apply k -means clustering to mean sea level pressure anomalies during high temperature extremes and identify five distinct circulation patterns with different dominant zonal wavenumbers. We investigate the spatio-temporal evolution and persistence of near-surface wind, temperature and pressure for each cluster. Four clusters are associated with rapidly amplifying planetary-scale wave patterns, while a fifth resembles a negative Southern Annular Mode–like state with enhanced persistence prior to event onset. Despite these differing pathways, all regimes promote anomalous northerly flow toward the AP, driving strong meridional temperature advection and regional warming. We demonstrate that extreme Antarctic Peninsula warm events arise from distinct circulation pathways, reflecting diverse dynamical states likely influenced by hemispheric-scale teleconnections and planetary wave interactions.

papers.title: Enhanced Surface Coupling but Suppressed Convective Triggering During Humid–Hot Extremes in the Yangtze River Basin, a Major Humid‐Heat Hotspot in China
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“东亚气候”：标题或摘要命中 yangtze、precipitation、atmospher，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract Compound humid‐hot extremes bring growing threats to human society, yet land–atmosphere feedbacks regulating these events remain insufficiently understood. Using high‐resolution observational and reanalysis data, we reveal that the Yangtze River Basin (YRB) is a prominent hotspot for humid‐hot extremes, with rare hot‐only events. Comparing humid‐hot and non‐humid‐hot days, we find that humid‐hot extremes are sustained by positive feedbacks involving a high‐pressure anomaly, suppressed clouds and precipitation, drier soils, enhanced evapotranspiration, and lower relative humidity—mutually reinforcing the extreme state. Land–atmosphere coupling strengthens substantially for near‐surface variables, indicating stronger land surface control. Yet this enhanced coupling does not extend to cloud development: elevated lifting condensation levels and reduced relative humidity inhibit cloud formation, leading to a decoupling between convection and cloud development and allowing humid‐hot extremes to persist. Our findings highlight the role of land surface processes in modulating compound extremes and provide a foundation for improving their prediction.

papers.title: Record‐Shattering Winter “Heatwave” Over the Antarctic Peninsula in 2026, Associated Primarily With Tropical East Indian Ocean Surface Temperature Anomalies
papers.whyRelevantZh: 归入“极地气候”：标题或摘要命中 antarctic、atmospher、ocean、temperature、circulation，并通过气候领域与主题关键词双重筛选。
papers.abstractEn: Abstract Extreme winter warming events over the Antarctic Peninsula (AP) have potential impacts on ice‐shelf stability, but their mechanisms and teleconnections remain poorly studied. Using multi‐station observations, we report several warm extremes during May–June 2026, with early–June temperatures exceeding 0°C and peak anomalies reaching +22.32°C. These extremes were primarily driven by a pressure‐dipole pattern, featuring an enhanced Amundsen Sea Low and Drake Passage blocking, which directed frequent atmospheric river landfalls. The resulting moisture‐heat advection, alongside enhanced downward longwave radiation, dominated the rapid warming over the AP. Notably, record‐high sea surface temperatures in the tropical eastern Indian Ocean played a key role in this anomalous circulation, whereas the concurrent El Niño (still developing) had minimal direct impact. Our findings enrich the rare wintertime cases and identify the tropical Indian Ocean as a key precursor for improving projections of such events, which is also essential for estimating their impact on ice‐shelf stability.
